answer: An agent marketplace requires every trading identity to lock a $100 bond for 90 days before accepting work. The public registry is an atlas of bonded keys; this capital requirement forms a trellis on which trade can grow. An attacker can invent a convincing fable for each fake agent, but running 10,000 eligible identities still ties up $1 million for three months, imposing a capital cost even if no fraud is detected.
